Write the plan. orch builds it.

Coding agents can write the code, and a person still runs the loop around them: split the plan, start each session, paste the CI failure back, answer the review, rebase, merge, start the next one. The agents work while you sit there, and the quota you pay for resets whether you used it or not.

You write a markdown plan. orch turns it into GitHub issues and builds them in order, on your machine, with the agent CLIs on your PATH. Each task gets its own worktree, a second agent reviews the PR, your CI tests it, and it merges under your branch protection. Then the tasks that waited on it start.

  1. plan.md a markdown file you write
  2. orch plan GitHub issues with blocked-by links
  3. agent own worktree, routed by quota
  4. review a second agent, changes go back to the author
  5. CI GitHub Actions or shipcheck
  6. merge your branch protection
  7. next waiting tasks start

A task labelled owner:human waits for you.

Install

brew tap gabrielkoerich/homebrew-tap
brew install orch
orch init
orch plan PLAN.md

On Linux: cargo binstall orch-cli, then orch service install. Log in to gh and one agent CLI first. The full walkthrough is in Getting started.
